lines.text: A picture book buried real gold.
In 1979, Kit Williams published a book called Masquerade.
lines.say: In nineteen seventy nine, Kit Williams published a book called Masquerade.

lines.text: Its paintings hid clues to a gold hare he made himself.
The hare had a ruby eye and tiny bells.
He sealed it in clay and wax to fool metal detectors.
He buried it beside a cross in Ampthill Park.
lines.say: He buried it beside a cross in Amt hill Park.

lines.text: It was found near the cross on February 24, 1982.
lines.say: It was found near the cross on February twenty fourth, nineteen eighty two.

lines.text: In 1988, Sotheby's sold it to a buyer overseas.
lines.say: In nineteen eighty eight, Sotheby's sold it to a buyer overseas.

lines.text: Then it vanished for more than twenty years.
A 2009 BBC appeal led its owners to bring it back.

post.caption: A picture book buried real gold. In 1979, Kit Williams published a book called Masquerade. Its paintings hid clues to a gold hare he made himself. The hare had a ruby eye and tiny bells. He sealed it in clay and wax to fool metal detectors. He buried it beside a cross in Ampthill Park. It was found near the cross on February 24, 1982. In 1988, Sotheby's sold it to a buyer overseas. Then it vanished for more than twenty years. A 2009 BBC appeal led its owners to bring it back.
